label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article II, Section 3. The President gives Congress information of the state of the Union and recommends measures to it; on extraordinary occasions he may convene both houses or either of them, and if they disagree about the time of adjournment he may adjourn them to such time as he thinks proper; he receives ambassadors and other public ministers, takes care that the laws be faithfully executed, and commissions all the officers of the United States.
This story is about an FBI investigation of a hack of the National Crime Information Center database.
In Federalist 69 (March 1788) Hamilton listed the duty "to take care that the laws be faithfully executed" among presidential powers that resemble those of the British king and the New York governor.

On September 25, 1794 Washington's Whiskey Rebellion proclamation, issued "in obedience to that high and irresistible duty consigned to me by the Constitution 'to take care that the laws be faithfully executed,'" declared that a force was already in motion to the scene of disaffection.
The FBI probes a hack of the NCIC, America's chief police database.
Stops and background checks usually match people against the NCIC.

The strongest argument against this is that probing a breach of a database is not itself the execution of any particular law, so this clause alone does not authorize an open investigation without a clearer duty already set by statute.
We read this clause to mean the executive must see that the laws are carried out in good faith.
Guarding the main tool for stops and checks protects how federal law is carried out.
Keeping that duty clear helps the laws work in daily life.
